ANNEX III
PROPERTIES OF WASTES WHICH RENDER THEM HAZARDOUS
H1 “Explosive”: substances and preparations which may explode under the effect of flame or which are more sensitive to shocks or friction than dinitrobenzene. H2 “Oxidizing”: substances and preparations which exhibit highly exothermic reactions when in contact with other substances, particularly flammable substances. H3-A
“Highly flammable”:
liquid substances and preparations having a flash point below 21C (including extremely flammable liquids), or
substances and preparations which may become hot and finally catch fire in contact with air at ambient temperature without any application of energy, or
solid substances and preparations which may readily catch fire after brief contact with a source of ignition and which continue to burn or to be consumed after removal of the source of ignition, or
gaseous substances and preparations which are flammable in air at normal pressure, or
substances and preparations which, in contact with water or damp air, evolve highly flammable gases in dangerous quantities.
H3-B “Flammable”: liquid substances and preparations having a flash point equal to or greater than 21°C and less than or equal to 55°C. H4 “Irritant”: non-corrosive substances and preparations which, through immediate, prolonged or repeated contact with the skin or mucous membrane, can cause inflammation. H5 “harmful”: substances and preparations which, if they are inhaled or ingested or if they penetrate the skin, may involve limited health risks. H6 “Toxic”: substances and preparations (including very toxic substances and preparations) which, if they are inhaled or ingested or if they penetrate the skin, may involve serious, acute or chronic health risks and even death. H7 “Carcinogenic”: substances and preparations which, if they are inhaled or ingested or if they penetrate the skin, may induce cancer or increase its incidence. H8 “Corrosive”: substances and preparations which may destroy living tissue on contacts. H9 “Infectious”: substances containing viable micro-organisms or their toxins which are known or reliably believed to cause disease in man or other living organisms. H10 “Teratogenic”: substances and preparations which, if they are inhaled or ingested or if they penetrate the skin, may induce non-hereditary congenital malformations or increase their incidence. H11 “Mutagenic”: substances and preparations which, if they are inhaled or ingested or if they penetrate the skin, may induce hereditary genetic defects or increase their incidence. H12 Substances and preparations which release toxic or very toxic gases in contact with water, air or an acid. H13 Substances and preparations capable by any means, after disposal, of yielding another substance, e.g. a leachate, which possesses any of the characteristics listed above. H14 “Ecotoxic”: substances and preparations which present or may present immediate or delayed risks for one or more sectors of the environment.
Notes
1
Attribution of the hazard properties “toxic” (and “very toxic”), “harmful”, “corrosive” and “irritant” is made on the basis of the criteria laid down by Annex VI, part I A and part II B, of Council Directive 67/548/EEC of 27 June 1967 of the approximation of laws, regulations and administrative provisions relating to the classification, packaging and labelling of dangerous substances , in the version as amended by Council Directive 79/831/EEC .
2
With regard to attribution of the properties “carcinogenic”, “teratogenic” and “mutagenic”, and reflecting the most recent findings, additional criteria are contained in the Guide to the classification and labelling of dangerous substances and preparations of Annex VI (part II D) to Directive 67/548/EEC in the version as amended by Commission Directive 83/467/EEC .
Test methods
The test methods serve to give specific meaning to the definitions given in Annex III.
The methods to be used are those described in Annex V to Directive 67/548/EEC , in the version as amended by Commission Directive 84/449/EEC , or by subsequent Commission Directives adapting Directive 67/548/EEC to technical progress. These methods are themselves based on the work and recommendations of the competent international bodies, in particular the OECD.

The Education (Acquisition of Grant–maintained Status) (Transitional Functions) Regulations 1993
In exercise of the powers conferred on the Secretary of State by section 301(6) of, and paragraphs 1 and 4 of Schedule 4 to, the Education Act 1993 , the Secretary of State for Education, as respects England, and the Secretary of State for Wales, as respects Wales, hereby make the following Regulations:
PART I
GENERAL
Citation and commencement
1
These Regulations may be cited as the Education (Acquisition of Grant– maintained Status) (Transitional Functions) Regulations 1993 and shall come into force on 1st January 1994.
Interpretation
2
In these Regulations —
“the 1993 Act ” means the Education Act 1993; and
“new governing body” shall be interpreted in accordance with section 34(2) of the 1993 Act.
PART II
CONTRACTS OF EMPLOYMENT
Application of Part II
3
1
This Part of these Regulations shall apply with respect to the exercise by the new governing body of a grant–maintained school of their powers under paragraph 2(a) of Schedule 4 to the 1993 Act to enter into a contract with a person for his employment as a member of staff at the school on or after the implementation date.
2
In this regulation, “implementation date” means the date specified as the proposed date of implementation in the proposals for acquisition of grant–maintained status published in relation to the school under section 32 of the 1993 Act.
Appointment of a prospective head teacher or deputy head teacher
4
1
This regulation applies to the exercise by the new governing body of a grant maintained school of their powers to enter into a contract of employment to which this Part of these Regulations applies where the person concerned is to be employed as the head or deputy head teacher of the school.
2
Before entering into any such contract with any person, the new governing body shall comply with the following provisions of this regulation with respect to the person’s appointment to the post of head teacher or, as the case may be, deputy head teacher.
3
The new governing body shall advertise the vacancy in such publications circulating throughout England and Wales as they consider appropriate.
4
The new governing body shall appoint a selection panel consisting of at least three of their members for the purpose of performing the functions conferred on the panel under paragraphs (5) and (6) below; and it shall be the duty of the new governing body to secure that the selection panel carry out the functions imposed on them under those paragraphs.
5
The selection panel shall —
a
interview such applicants for the post as they think fit; and
b
where they consider that it is appropriate to do so, recommend to the new governing body for appointment one of the applicants interviewed by them.
6
Where —
a
the selection panel are unable to agree on a person to recommend to the new governing body of a grant–maintained school, or the new governing body do not approve their recommendation; and
b
the new governing body (whether or not they re–advertise the vacancy in accordance with paragraph (3) above) request the panel to repeat the steps mentioned in paragraph (5) above,
the panel shall repeat the steps mentioned in that paragraph.
Appointment of staff other than the head teacher and deputy head teacher
5
1
This regulation applies to the exercise by the new governing body of a grant– maintained school of their powers to enter into a contract of employment to which this Part of these Regulations applies where the person concerned is to be employed otherwise than as the head or deputy head teacher of the school.
2
Before entering into any such contract with any person, the new governing body shall comply with the following provisions of this regulation with respect to the person’s appointment.
3
Subject to paragraph (4) below, the new governing body shall, before determining to appoint any person, consider any advice given by —
a
any person who has been appointed by the new governing body to be the head teacher of the school from a date beginning on or after the implementation date; or
b
if there is no such person, the existing head teacher of the school.
4
The new governing body may delegate to the person referred to in paragraph (3)(a) above or, if there is no such person, the person referred to in paragraph (3)(b) above the function of selecting a person to be considered by them for appointment; and in those circumstances paragraph (3) above shall not apply.
5
Subject to paragraph (6) below, before appointing any person to a teaching post at the school the new governing body shall, unless they decide to fill the vacancy by the appointment of a person who is already employed to work at the school, advertise the vacancy as they think fit.
6
Where the new governing body advertise a vacancy in accordance with paragraph (5) above, they shall not be required to appoint a person who has applied for the vacancy in response to their advertisement.
Form of contract of employment
6
Any contract of employment to which this Part of these Regulations applies shall be in writing.
PART III
PROVISION OF INFORMATION
Information which may be requested by the new governing body
7
1
For the purposes of paragraph 4(1) of Schedule 4 to the 1993 Act, the information which may be requested by the new governing body of a grant–maintained school is —
a
any information held by the existing governing body of the school or, as the case may be, the local education authority by whom the school is maintained relating to the persons employed to work at the school;
b
any information so held relating to any property (including premises) held or used for the purposes of the school;
c
any information so held relating to expenditure by the existing governing body of any sums made available to them in respect of the school’s budget share for the financial year in which the request is made;
d
any information so held relating to any contract entered into, or proposed to be entered into, by the existing governing body or (as the case may be) the local education authority which would or might bind the new governing body when the school becomes grant–maintained; and
e
any information held by the existing governing body of the school relating to the pupils at the school, including in particular the names and addresses of their parents.
2
In this regulation —
“financial year” means a period of twelve months ending with 31st March; and
“school’s budget share” shall be interpreted in accordance with section 51(2)(b) of the Education Reform Act 1988 .
John Patten
Secretary of State for Education
3rd December 1993
John Redwood
Secretary of State for Wales
